name: Stanford HAI AI Index: landing page for annual AI trends report
title: Stanford HAI AI Index: landing page for annual AI trends report
answer: The Stanford HAI AI Index is an independent initiative that publishes an annual report tracking, collating, distilling, and visualizing data on artificial intelligence. Its landing page says the latest edition, the seventh and the 2024 Index, reveals a widening gap between what AI can do and how prepared we are to manage it. It claims the report covers technical progress, economic influence, and societal impact through a cross-sector lens. For nonprofit readers it offers macro context and an authoritative reference, but it does not discuss nonprofits directly.

sections.body: Stanford HAI publishes this AI Index landing page. It describes the AI Index as an independent initiative at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence, led by an interdisciplinary AI Index Steering Committee. The page presents the AI Index as an annual report that tracks, collates, distills, and visualizes data relating to artificial intelligence. It states that the seventh edition is the 2024 Index and calls it the most comprehensive to date. The page also links to people, a related measurement paper from a fall 2019 Stanford workshop, a collaboration on AI regulatory frameworks, and a philanthropic support page. It is a descriptive landing page rather than the full report.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page says the AI Index mission is to provide unbiased, rigorously vetted, and globally sourced data for policymakers, researchers, journalists, executives, and the general public. It tracks, collates, distills, and visualizes data relating to artificial intelligence. This year's Index, according to the page, reveals a widening gap between what AI can do and how prepared we are to manage it. AI is integrating rapidly into the global economy, with technical capabilities improving, investment accelerating, and adoption spreading, while frameworks to govern, evaluate, and understand the technology fall behind. In a field where data transparency is declining, the page argues independent, rigorous measurement is critical. Stanford HAI says AI is poised to be the most transformative technology of the 21st century, but its benefits will not be evenly distributed unless development is guided thoughtfully. The AI Index is presented as a comprehensive, data-driven view of AI, recognized by global media, governments, and leading companies. It aims to equip policymakers, business leaders, and the public with insights into technical progress, economic influence, and societal impact. Previous editions were cited in The New York Times, Bloomberg, and The Guardian, amassed hundreds of academic citations, and were referenced by high-level policymakers in the United States, the United Kingdom, and the European Union. It writes about AI through a cross-sector lens, from research and development to technical performance, the economy, education, policy, and more.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that this is the seventh edition and the 2024 Index. It says previous editions were cited in The New York Times, Bloomberg, and The Guardian, amassed hundreds of academic citations, and were referenced by high-level policymakers in the United States, the United Kingdom, and the European Union. It describes a related paper based on a fall 2019 Stanford workshop that identifies six summary challenges and summarizes over 40 presentations. It also states that the AI Index is an independent initiative at Stanford HAI, led by an interdisciplinary Steering Committee, and that Stanford HAI relies on philanthropic support. It gives no nonprofit-specific numbers or definitions.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in nonprofits would use this source as macro context and as a citable reference for AI's technical progress, economic influence, and societal impact. The page says the AI Index is recognized by global media, governments, and leading companies, and that it writes through a cross-sector lens that includes education and policy. That can help nonprofit staff frame funding proposals, policy comments, or public communications with authoritative background. However, the source does not discuss nonprofits, charities, mission-driven organizations, or public-sector implementation, so it cannot support claims about nonprofit adoption or impact. It is best treated as a general AI trends source, not a nonprofit sector source.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Nonprofits

sections.body: This is a landing page, not the full AI Index report, and much of the text is descriptive or promotional. It does not provide methodology, data tables, or findings by sector. It does not mention nonprofits, charities, mission-driven organizations, or public-sector organizations. The stated edition is the 2024 Index, while the page was harvested in 2026, so it may not reflect the latest edition. It is published by Stanford HAI and notes philanthropic support, but the text does not show commercial sponsorship. The page is partial and should be read alongside the actual report for substantive data.
